codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL CODE QUALITY ISSUES: This code contains 3 critical SQL injection vulnerabilities in all three new functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) caused by direct string interpolation in SQL queries. These vulnerabilities can allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands, delete data, or extract sensitive information. The code violates the established security patterns already in use within the codebase (parameterized queries in createTodo/getTodoById), indicating inadequate code review. Additional issues include missing input validation, type safety violations, poor error handling, performance concerns with unoptimized LIKE queries, and inadequate documentation.

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodos(): User input (keyword) is directly interpolated into SQL query using template literal without parameterization or sanitization. Attacker can inject arbitrary SQL by providing keywords like '; DROP TABLE todos; --'
issues.suggestion: Replace template literal with parameterized query: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $2'; const params = [`%${keyword}%`, `%${keyword}%`]; const rows = await db.query(query, params);

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodos(): Direct string interpolation in WHERE clause is OWASP Top 10 vulnerability. The pattern `LIKE '%${keyword}%'` is exploitable regardless of keyword content.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries with placeholders ($1, $2) as demonstrated in existing secure functions like createTodo() and getTodoById()

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus(): User input (completed) is concatenated directly without type checking or parameterization. An attacker could pass '1; DELETE FROM todos; --' to execute arbitrary commands.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: const sql = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const rows = await db.query(sql, [completed]);

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus(): String concatenation operator (+) used instead of parameterized queries, making this function exploitable for privilege escalation or data deletion attacks.
issues.suggestion: Refactor to use parameterized query with proper type casting: const sql = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const rows = await db.query(sql, [completed === 'true']);

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser(): User ID is interpolated directly into template literal without parameterization. An attacker can inject SQL through userId parameter.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1'; const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]);

issues.description: Pattern inconsistency: This function violates the established secure pattern used by createTodo() and getTodoById() in the same codebase, both of which use parameterized queries. This inconsistency signals technical debt and increases maintenance risk.
issues.suggestion: Standardize all database queries to use parameterized queries with placeholder syntax ($1, $2, etc.) consistently across the module

issues.description: No input validation on keyword parameter in searchTodos(). Empty strings, null, undefined, or excessively long strings (>10000 chars) could cause performance degradation or unexpected behavior.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (!keyword || typeof keyword !== 'string' || keyword.trim().length === 0) throw new Error('Invalid keyword'); if (keyword.length > 255) throw new Error('Keyword too long');

issues.description: Type mismatch vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus(): completed parameter is typed as string but SQL expects boolean. No validation ensures the value is 'true' or 'false', allowing injection of any string value into the WHERE clause.
issues.suggestion: Change signature to: searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]> and update calls accordingly

issues.description: No validation of userId format in getTodosByUser(). UUIDs or numeric IDs should be validated against expected format before use in SQL query to catch malformed requests early.
issues.suggestion: Add format validation before query execution to ensure userId matches expected pattern

issues.description: LIKE queries with leading wildcard ('%${keyword}%') cannot efficiently use B-tree indexes, resulting in full table scans even on large datasets. This can cause significant performance degradation as todos table grows.
issues.suggestion: Consider using full-text search (FTS) or trigram indexes (pg_trgm in PostgreSQL) for better performance on LIKE queries with wildcards. Document expected result limits in JSDoc.

issues.description: searchTodos() searches both title AND description fields with OR operator on unindexed columns. This multiplies the search cost and may timeout on large datasets without proper indexing strategy.
issues.suggestion: Add indexes on (title) and (description) columns. Document expected performance characteristics. Consider limiting results: LIMIT 100 with pagination for better UX.

issues.description: No JSDoc parameter documentation or return type details. The function lacks error documentation (what exceptions might be thrown?) and doesn't explain query limits or pagination expectations.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive JSDoc documentation covering parameters, return values, exceptions, and examples

issues.description: Function naming is ambiguous: searchTodosByStatus() doesn't indicate what statuses are valid or whether it expects 'true'/'false' strings or boolean values. The string parameter type makes the contract unclear.
issues.suggestion: Rename to filterTodosByCompletion() or filterTodosByCompletionStatus() and change parameter type to boolean

issues.description: No error handling in any of the three functions. If db.query() fails, the error propagates uncaught, potentially exposing database connection strings or internal structure in error messages.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch blocks with appropriate error handling and context wrapping

issues.description: Inconsistent return type assertion in searchTodos(). Using 'as Todo[]' bypasses TypeScript type checking and could hide mismatches between database schema and Todo interface.
issues.suggestion: Add type guard function to validate results before returning

issues.description: Inconsistent SQL formatting: searchTodosByStatus() uses string concatenation while searchTodos() uses template literals. This style inconsistency reduces code readability and increases error likelihood.
issues.suggestion: Use consistent SQL query construction across the module with parameterized queries

issues.description: Comments with emoji warnings (⚠️, ❌) and 'VULNERABLE' labels suggest this code was written with known security issues or as a teaching example. This should not be merged to production without fixes.
issues.suggestion: Remove warning comments and implement proper security fixes before merge

testCoverage.summary: The three new functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) have zero test coverage. Critical security vulnerabilities are present but untested: SQL injection risks in all three functions due to string concatenation in SQL queries without parameterized statement protection. No tests exist to verify secure query construction. Essential edge cases are completely untested: empty/null/undefined inputs, special SQL characters, very long strings, and database error handling. The searchTodosByStatus function's type contract is ambiguous (string parameter for boolean-like status). Until comprehensive test suites covering these areas exist and pass, these functions should not be used in production.

untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call searchTodos(null as any) and searchTodos(undefined as any). Verify graceful error handling.

refactorings.summary: Seven critical refactoring opportunities identified, primarily focused on eliminating SQL injection vulnerabilities, fixing type safety issues, and aligning with secure patterns already established in the codebase. The main issues are: (1) All three search functions use string interpolation instead of parameterized queries, violating the secure pattern established by createTodo and getTodoById; (2) searchTodosByStatus accepts string parameter for boolean-like status, creating type safety issues; (3) No input validation on any of the three functions; (4) Inconsistent error handling; (5) Duplicate query execution logic across functions; (6) Missing documentation and error context. Refactoring will bring functions into alignment with secure, maintainable patterns.

recommendations.description: DO NOT MERGE: All three new functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) contain SQL injection vulnerabilities from direct string interpolation in SQL queries. This is a critical security issue that violates OWASP Top 10 standards. Immediately refactor to use parameterized queries with placeholders ($1, $2, etc.) as demonstrated in existing secure functions (createTodo, getTodoById, deleteTodo).

Zero test coverage for new functions: The three new search functions have no tests. Combined with SQL injection vulnerabilities, this represents unacceptable risk. Create comprehensive test suites covering SQL injection attempts, edge cases (null/undefined/empty values), special SQL characters, invalid inputs, and database error scenarios before merge.

Fix type mismatch in searchTodosByStatus(): The 'completed' parameter is typed as string but semantically represents a boolean completion status. Change parameter type to boolean to align with TypeScript best practices and prevent injection of arbitrary string values. This will also require updating all call sites.

Add input validation to all three functions: No validation exists for keyword (searchTodos), status (searchTodosByStatus), or userId (getTodosByUser). Add explicit checks for empty, null, undefined, and excessively long values. Follow the pattern established by validateTodoInput() already in the codebase.

Align with established secure patterns: The codebase already demonstrates secure SQL patterns in createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, and deleteTodo using parameterized queries. The new functions violate this pattern. Refactoring to match established patterns will improve maintainability and security consistency.

Optimize LIKE queries: The searchTodos() function uses LIKE with leading wildcards ('%keyword%') which prevents efficient B-tree index usage and causes full table scans. Consider using full-text search indexes (PostgreSQL FTS or trigram indexes) for better performance on large datasets.

Add structured error handling: None of the three functions have try-catch blocks. Database errors propagate uncaught, potentially exposing sensitive information. Add error handling patterns consistent with the codebase conventions.

Extract common query patterns: The repeated db.query() and type casting pattern across all three functions suggests an opportunity to extract a shared utility function (executeTodoQuery) to reduce duplication and centralize error handling.

Add JSDoc comments: The functions lack comprehensive documentation of parameters, return values, exceptions, and usage examples. Add JSDoc following the pattern established elsewhere in the codebase to improve discoverability and IDE support.
